issues.failure_explanation: The main-text update uses Pi_t as Lambda_t^{-1}, but for the displayed Lambda_t in Appendix \ref{appendix:1}, Lambda_t^{-1} has (1,1) entry -a_t, not +a_t. With +a_t, the Woodbury step is not the inverse of \hat{\Xi}_{t+1}=\frac{t}{t+1}(\hat{\Xi}_t+R_t\Lambda_tR_t^T).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the (1,1) entry of Pi_t from a_t to -a_t, equivalently replace Pi_t by Lambda_t^{-1}=[[-a_t,1,0],[1,0,0],[0,0,t\varphi_t]] as derived in Appendix \ref{appendix:1}.
issues.overall_effect: The stated fully online update of \hat{\Xi}_t^{-1} is incorrect as written; using it would corrupt the confidence-region computation. Corollary \ref{sec4:cor1} itself remains a coverage statement and is not invalidated, since the correct inverse recursion is derived in Appendix \ref{appendix:1}.
issues.title: Wrong sign in the online inverse-covariance update
issues.why_classification: The repair is a single forced sign correction and the Appendix already contains the correct Sherman-Morrison-Woodbury recursion, so all stated guarantees survive.

failure_location.quote: Notably, Theorem \ref{sec4:thm1} does~not~\mbox{require}~$B_t$~to~\mbox{converge}~to~the true Hessian $\nabla^2 F(\tx)$, making our analysis directly applicable to conditioned SGD methods.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Qualify the bullet: state that the Hessian-average case is covered by Theorem \ref{sec4:thm1} and Lemma \ref{sec4:lem1}, while a general preconditioner with a non-Hessian limit requires a separate covariance analysis.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised direct applicability to conditioned SGD methods such as AdaGrad, RMSProp, and quasi-Newton methods is unsupported. A reader could wrongly apply \hat{\Xi}_t to a method whose limiting preconditioner is not the Hessian; the sketched-Newton results themselves are not damaged.
issues.title: Unsupported claim of direct applicability to conditioned SGD
issues.why_classification: The fix is a limited weakening/qualification of an overclaim, but substantiating the claimed generalization to non-Hessian preconditioners would require a new argument rather than a local correction.
